rationale: X is at overall parity with the references: it frames the developer-visible uncertainty rather than prematurely choosing last-good routes versus fail-until-fixed, and it covers every requested actor, boundary, configuration, edge case, open question, and evidence need. Its source-based account of clear-before-load, shared application and engine reloading, watcher state consumption, lazy initial loading, and request-cycle behavior under both reload settings agrees with the checkout, while clearly marking untested failure behavior as inference. It is slightly less decisive about immediate recovery after correction and performs no live reproduction, but the references likewise leave that behavior to future evidence, so neither limitation is a material error.

shortcomings.summary: No live failure-path reproduction was executed
shortcomings.evidence: X explicitly says it did not boot an app and break a live routes.rb, so the central sequence of bad save, following request, and correction remains source-derived rather than observed at the HTTP boundary.

shortcomings.summary: The correction example leaves a little avoidable ambiguity
shortcomings.evidence: Acceptance example 5 says the next request 'that is supposed to see file changes' should recover and entertains a documented full reload cycle, whereas the strongest user-facing target is recovery on the next watcher-visible request without a dummy edit or restart.

strengths.summary: It distinguishes established behavior from consequential inference
strengths.evidence: X separately lists behavior established by tests and labels clear-before-load, consumed watcher state, and post-failure retry behavior as inferred and not reproduced, avoiding an unsupported categorical diagnosis.

strengths.summary: It covers the full requested behavior matrix without prescribing a solution
strengths.evidence: The brief includes valid and invalid initial boot, failed reload and following request, correction, simultaneous app and engine edits, deletion, external draw files, both reload_classes_only_on_change values, custom watchers, non-goals, and open product questions.

strengths.summary: Its technical boundary and key claims match the Rails source
strengths.evidence: RoutesReloader clears all registered route sets before loading paths; Engine registers application and engine paths and external directories on the shared application reloader; FileUpdateChecker advances watched state before invoking the reload block; and finisher.rb checks watchers when reload_classes_only_on_change is true but runs each request cycle when false.
